title: Shipped default witness configuration
statement: Ship a default the project neither operates nor overloads: an RFC 3161 timestamp authority for the per-batch countersignature and clock, plus a trust-minimised roll-up anchor on a slow interval. A transparency log such as Rekor is opt-in — for operators self-hosting one, or whose volume suits a public instance — and never the shipped default, because a 10-second cadence against a public good is not acceptable use.
source: Independence — the shipped default anchors to a log we do not run
verify: Default config asserted in test; a day of operation produces no more than the configured roll-up count against any public service

title: Documented CLI contract
statement: Provide the entry points and flags printed in Getting started: collect-oma, mcp-proxy (--upstream, --out), verify (--policy), coverage (--from, --to) and disclose (--event, --out).
source: Getting started — the published commands
verify: CLI contract test executes every documented invocation verbatim

title: Witness publishes signed tree heads
statement: The witness publishes its own signed tree head so an operator or third party can detect a rolled-back or equivocating witness.
source: Durability — losing a witness must not lose the evidence
verify: Rollback simulation: a witness serving an earlier head is detected

title: Witness key rotation
statement: Rotate witness keys while keeping historical countersignatures verifiable, by publishing a signed key history.
source: Durability — key rotation
verify: Countersignatures from a retired key still verify after rotation

title: Build provenance attestation
statement: Publish a provenance attestation for every released collector artifact, binding the digest to its source commit and build, so the digest in a heartbeat can be independently traced.
source: Provenance — a build digest you can check
verify: Attestation verifies against the published artifact and source revision

title: Signed releases and SBOM
statement: Sign every release and publish an SBOM with pinned dependencies.
source: Provenance — signed releases and an SBOM
verify: Signature and SBOM present and verified in CI for each release

title: Key compromise recovery
statement: Document and support recovery from operator key compromise: a declared, countersigned discontinuity rather than a silent re-key.
source: Durability — key compromise
verify: Compromise drill: discontinuity is recorded, countersigned and visible to the verifier

title: Witness time source
statement: The witness clock derives from a documented, traceable time source, and the verifier surfaces the witness's declared time discipline.
source: Durability — the clock the witness stamps with
verify: Time source documented; drift monitored and alerted

title: Witness store durability
statement: The witness store is replicated and recoverable, with a documented recovery point objective, because a witness that loses its roots destroys the corroboration it exists to provide.
source: Durability — losing a witness must not lose the evidence
verify: Restore drill from backup; RPO measured against the stated objective

title: No agent code changes
statement: Both collectors integrate by dependency and configuration only; no change to the customer's agent code is required.
source: Why — without asking you to change your agent code
verify: Byte-identical agent source before and after integration, for both collectors

title: WPS states the time discipline
statement: The practice statement names the witness's time source and the limits of the time assertion.
source: Witness Practice Statement — per its clock
verify: Statement text reviewed against SEC-25 implementation

title: Bounty: cash deferred until funded
statement: State publicly that a cash award opens only if the project is funded, rather than promising money that is not held.
source: Resourcing
verify: Terms published with the condition stated; no figure advertised as available

title: Accept third-party attack classes
statement: Accept contributed attack classes by pull request, with attribution. A goal, explicitly not a launch gate.
source: Attack class section — the suite is open, contributions are invited
verify: Contribution path documented; not referenced in any release gate

title: No fail-closed option
statement: MUST NOT provide any configuration, flag or build that makes the collector block an agent run. Fail-open is a design constraint, not a setting.
source: Operations — a design constraint, not a setting
verify: Config schema review; no enforcement path exists; rejected as a feature request by policy

title: State the resourcing honestly
statement: Publish that the project is unfunded and what that means: no hosted witness, no accreditation, no certification mark, and recognition rather than cash. Stated plainly rather than implied by omission.
source: Resourcing
verify: Section present in the release notes and the README
evidence: Resourcing section in README and notes

title: Canonicalisation completeness
statement: The canonical encoding must cover every field of the action record at every nesting depth. A test must prove that mutating any single field, at any depth, changes the leaf digest.
source: Capture — action record: tool name, arguments, result, approval decision
verify: Property test mutating each field in turn, including nested argument keys; every mutation must change the digest

title: Roll-up anchoring
statement: Anchor a periodic summary checkpoint covering many batches, separately from the per-batch soft anchor, so a public or rate-limited witness receives a handful of entries per day rather than thousands.
source: Independence — tiered anchoring
verify: A day of 10-second batches produces one roll-up entry per configured interval, and the roll-up proves inclusion of every batch beneath it

title: Cross-pack consistency verification
statement: Given two or more evidence packs, detect a record inconsistent with a checkpoint already countersigned in an earlier pack — so a record truncated below a height previously disclosed is contradicted offline, with no live service.
source: Proof — offline verification; Durability
verify: Disclose at seq 5000, truncate to 4799, compare the two packs: the earlier countersigned checkpoint contradicts the later record

title: Counterparty reference capture
statement: Extract externally issued identifiers from a tool result and index them for reconciliation. The index lives in the deletable content store, never in the chain, because a transaction reference can itself be identifying.
source: Capture — action record
verify: A result containing an external reference is indexed and queryable; the index is removed by crypto-shredding

title: Resist truncation below a disclosed height
statement: A record truncated below a sequence already disclosed in a countersigned pack must be detectable by comparing the two, without any stateful witness.
source: Attack class table, rows 4 and 5
verify: Red-team class I: truncate below a disclosed height; cross-pack comparison fails closed

title: Reconciliation guidance
statement: Document reconciliation against counterparty records as a detection method for erasure and omission, with its limits stated: it requires access to the counterparty and it is a procedure an auditor performs, not a guarantee the software makes.
source: Durability; Threat model — residual risk
verify: Guidance published; the limits appear wherever the method is claimed

title: Collector instance identity
statement: Each collector instance has a stable identity that scopes its chain and its log origin. Records carry the run they belong to as a field; the chain itself is collector-scoped, so concurrent runs interleave in one log and heartbeats need no run at all.
source: Capture — action record; Coverage attestation
verify: Two concurrent runs produce one contiguous chain with correct run tags; a heartbeat emitted with no run active is chained and anchored

title: Document the collector-patch limit
statement: State plainly, wherever coverage attestation is described, that a collector patched to report a valid digest while suppressing actions is not detectable without remote attestation, which this release does not provide.
source: Coverage attestation; Threat model — residual risk
verify: Statement present in the threat model, the coverage report output, and DES-10; claims audit checks no surface implies otherwise

title: Verifier states witness-set capabilities
statement: The verifier prints what the configured or observed witness set can and cannot establish — in particular whether any witness maintains operator sequence state, and therefore whether truncation above the last disclosed height is detectable at all.
source: Proof — offline verification; Independence
verify: Test asserts a stateless witness set yields an explicit "truncation not detectable above <height>" line, and a stateful one does not

title: Reserved slot for gap declarations
statement: Pre-allocate storage sufficient to write a gap declaration, so the declaration can be written even when the store is otherwise exhausted. If even that fails, the condition is surfaced out of band and the next successful write declares the lost window.
source: Operations — fails open, loudly
verify: Disk-exhaustion test: the agent completes, a gap declaration is written from the reserve, and the lost window appears in the coverage report

title: Action record and chain entry are separate structures
statement: The canonicalised, hashed ActionRecord is immutable and contains no chain metadata. prev, leaf and head live in a ChainEntry wrapper that is never canonicalised, so the digest of a record can never depend on a value derived from it. Conformance vectors publish the exact bytes hashed.
source: Integrity — chained, salted, ratcheted; Capture — action record
verify: Conformance vectors: given a fixed ActionRecord, the canonical bytes, leaf and head are byte-exact. A test asserts no chain field appears inside the canonicalised subject

title: Unknown-loss intervals
statement: When the observation counter did not survive — an unrecoverable crash with the counter only in memory — declare an unknown-loss interval bounded by the last durable checkpoint and the first record after restart. Never fabricate an exact span. The two kinds of loss evidence are distinct record kinds and a verifier reports them differently.
source: Operations — fails open, loudly; Coverage attestation
verify: Disk exhaustion followed by kill -9 and restart: an unknown-loss interval is written with no span, and no exact gap is invented. A verifier distinguishes it from a declared span

title: Observation counter durability
statement: Checkpoint the observation counter durably at each batch flush, so an unrecoverable crash loses at most the current window and the unknown-loss interval is bounded rather than open-ended.
source: Operations — fails open, loudly
verify: Kill -9 mid-window: the restart reads the last checkpointed source_seq and the declared unknown interval starts there, not at zero
